summary: MISO answers the 21 comments and protests on its LARS filing, defending the Local Resource Zone proximity test, 200 MW threshold, 15-year pairing and application role of the Transmission Customer, and says it will fold in cost reforms due November 16.
ask: Accept the answer and accept the LARS filing as proposed, so MISO can implement LARS in the first quarter of 2027.

points.point: MISO says LARS responds to the show cause order and should not wait for the large load cost reforms due November 16.
points.quote: such a delay would frustrate the goals of the Show Cause Order and needlessly sacrifice the benefits of critical reforms for ratepayers and stakeholders without corresponding benefit.

points.point: MISO says the Local Resource Zone fits its system and the order invited tailoring the proximity definition.
points.quote: MISO is expanding upon the Commission's definition to fit its needs and resource adequacy construct.

points.point: MISO describes its zone test as electrically proximate plus because it rewards close siting and also serves pairs farther apart.
points.quote: MISO's LRZ approach thus can be considered an "electrically proximate plus" construct

points.point: MISO says LARS creates no new cost shift, and the Transmission Customer stays liable for assigned projects even if the load never starts service.
points.quote: LARS does not create any new cost shift opportunities, but LARS does mitigate risks that already exist.

points.point: MISO and the Transmission Owners will file pro forma cost recovery agreements by November 16, 2026, and MISO would accept a compliance directive to fold them into LARS.
points.quote: MISO is willing to accept a compliance directive requiring such a filing should the Commission deem this necessary.

points.point: MISO says LARS will not take headroom from DPP queue projects because LARS models are built on the existing MTEP model.
points.quote: each LARS study cycle model will be built based on the existing MTEP model, which would not remove any available headroom from active DPP queue projects

points.point: MISO rejects the gatekeeper charge: only Transmission Customers have been able to submit EPR requests, and an unpaired generator would make LARS speculative.
points.quote: LARS is a load-driven process, and an Interconnection Customer cannot require a Transmission Customer to scope their Transmission Service request around a generator they have not chosen to pair with.

points.point: MISO opposes a sunset date but commits to post pair data each cycle and to review usage regularly.
points.quote: MISO commits to publicly post, at the beginning of each LARS cycle, information on each LARS generation/load pair's POI and POW

points.point: MISO defends the 200 MW floor and the 15-year pairing as ways to keep LARS for the largest, committed pairs.
points.quote: The 15-year minimum pairing of the generation and load pairs in LARS is a necessary aspect of ensuring certainty for MISO

throughLine.text: MISO replies in its section 205 LARS docket to protests that LARS only partly answers the E-8 show cause order on proximity and cost shifting, and points to its November 16 cost recovery agreement filing.
